title: Signed total Cech pairing axis formulas
statement: Given any scheme X, any family U of opens (no covering hypothesis), any computing sectionwise resolution pairing D [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data], comparison data A,B,C [def-sc-cech-cup-resolution-comparison-data] for its three resolutions, and natural degrees p,q, there exists a global-section-linear bilinear map on total homology in degrees p,q to degree p+q. It carries H(alpha) of paired global resolution cycles to H(alpha) of the target cycle, and H(beta) of coefficient Cech cycles to H(beta) of their Alexander-Whitney product [def-sc-cech-cup-product]. Both formulas quantify over all target kernel cycles with the stated underlying paired cochain. No compatibility on sheaf cohomology is assumed.

proof.text: On input bidegrees (r,i),(s,j), use front/back restrictions, apply the supplied D.pair on the common intersection and multiply by (-1)^(i*s). Assemble over the finite total-degree summands. Expand the alternating Cech differential as in cechCupCochain_leibniz: all shared-vertex terms cancel, and restriction compatibility and bilinearity permit the same calculation for D.pair. Combine with D.leibniz; the factor (-1)^(i*s) makes the resolution-first total differential satisfy the total Leibniz identity. Cycles pair to cycles, and pairing a boundary with a cycle is a boundary by that identity. Thus quotient descent gives the bilinear map on homology.

On alpha images both Cech degrees are zero, so the sign is one and D.restriction identifies the pairing with restriction of paired global sections. On beta images both resolution degrees are zero, so the sign is one and D.augmentation_pair identifies the pairing with augmentation of cechCupCochain. Use alpha_f and beta_f and pass these two cochain equalities to classes. Neither Godement construction nor existence of a new resolution pairing is used.

theorem cupCechResolution_total_pairing {X : Scheme.{v}} {ι : Type v}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) {F G : X.Modules} (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
    (A : CupCechResolutionComparison U D.left)
    (B : CupCechResolutionComparison U D.right)
    (C : CupCechResolutionComparison U D.target) (p q : ℕ) :
    ∃ t : ((cupCechDouble U D.left.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).homology p →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
      ((cupCechDouble U D.right.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).homology q →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
        ((cupCechDouble U D.target.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).homology (p + q),
      (∀ (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val →
          t (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap A.alpha p (cupCycleClass _ p a))
              (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap B.alpha q (cupCycleClass _ q b)) =
            HomologicalComplex.homologyMap C.alpha (p + q) (cupCycleClass _ (p + q) c)) ∧
      (∀ (a : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).sc
          p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj G.presheafModuleCat).sc
          q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj (F ⊗ G).presheafModuleCat).sc
          (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c.val = cechCupCochain U F G p q a.val b.val →
          t (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap A.beta p (cupCycleClass _ p a))
              (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap B.beta q (cupCycleClass _ q b)) =
            HomologicalComplex.homologyMap C.beta (p + q) (cupCycleClass _ (p + q) c))
